Seventeen comments

Donegal Tinker

This is a mighty tune taken from Cathal Hayden’s “Cathal Hayden” CD, first tune, track 4. The second tune on that track is the Dublin Reel. Together they rock. Donegal Tinker is listed as a Gmaj tune, but it may be a Dmix. Either way, the key signature works.

↳ Posted by banjoscout on June 21st, 2003.

It sounds like a member of the Tinker family (Drunken, Jolly and Yellow).

↳ Posted by CreadurMawnOrganig on June 22nd, 2003.

Donegal tinker

So, what IS it about those tinker tunes??….they all rock. This one, in particular, has been a favourite of mine since I first started playing it last summer….It’s one of those big tunes that seem to have an epic sort of quality.

↳ Posted by aoife on June 23rd, 2003.

Dang, that’s a fine tune. Just added it to the old tunebook. Might try slapping it together with Cuillian Vallely’s “Singing Stream”. It has a similar energy.

↳ Posted by Kerri Coombs on May 11th, 2004.

Kerri, have a listen to track 4 at http://www.woodstockrecords.com/cathal_cd.html ! Damn fine playing, too…

↳ Posted by Zina Lee on May 11th, 2004.

The Donegal Tinker, X:8

Here’s a lovely piping setting from the playing of piper Liam Winnett. I’ve put D major in the header and notated the many C naturals, as one of the pipey characteristics is the contrast between the c# and the C natural. Of course, what he does is more complex than this.
Here’s a link (it’s to his FB page): https://fb.watch/GT6JV_EZfs/?
